description: Dependency update pull requests for wordpress-nginx, on the shared preset of ioanalytica/renovate-config (schedule, minimum release age, DCO, review requests, the label decision): GitHub Actions and the tools the workflows install, the Dockerfiles' base images, the third-party images the chart pins, the documentation site's npm packages. WordPress and Dragonfly have their own workflows (wp-version-check.yml, dragonfly-version-check.yml), and the wordpress-idx submodule moves by hand. The hash pins that go with a version pin are .github/checksums.yaml's: the workflow pin-checksums.yml fills them on the bot's branch. tests/ci/test.sh guards what the bot updates and what stays manual.

git-submodules.description: The wordpress-idx pin moves by hand: each move is a change to the search sidecar's image, with its line in chart/CHANGELOG.md.

helm-values.description: The image pins of the chart's own values file only, not of examples or fixtures.

helmv3.description: The common chart dependency moves with the chart's releases.

customManagers.description: Tool versions of the workflows, an env *_VERSION under a '# renovate: datasource=... depName=...' line.

The entries of the third-party images in the list Artifact Hub reads (artifacthub.io/images in chart/Chart.yaml), under the names the helm-values manager gives the same images in chart/values.yaml, so that one pull request moves both spots; the template test fails when they differ.
Runner labels of a job matrix (build-image.yml, release.yml): the github-actions manager reads runners in runs-on only.
The k3s image the page Try it locally creates its k3d cluster with; try-locally.yml runs the page's command. Only releases: no rc tags, no tags of one architecture.

packageRules.description: Release tags of the pinned tools carry a v prefix, the pins do not.

The preset this file extends and the workflow pin-checksums.yml calls, both of ioanalytica/renovate-config, move in one pull request. The preset has this group too, but its rules come before this file's: here, after the group GitHub Actions, it wins for the workflow's pin.
The runner labels of a matrix go with the runs-on ones; a new major shares their branch by its name.
The Renovate that renovate-config.yml runs, once a month: Renovate releases most days.
The k3d of the job try-locally.yml; its pull request runs that job.
prBodyNotes: For a new minor, tests/try-locally/test.sh fails until "Tested with k3d …" in examples/k3d/README.md names it.

packageRules.description: The k3s of the page Try it locally; its pull request runs the job try-locally.yml.
prBodyNotes: For a new minor, tests/try-locally/test.sh fails until "Tested with k3d … and k3s …" in examples/k3d/README.md names it.

packageRules.description: Dragonfly has its own workflow, dragonfly-version-check.yml: it proposes a version only after a container has started with the flags the chart passes.
A change to an image the chart runs by default is a change to the chart.
prBodyNotes: This changes an image the chart pins: add a line under `## Unreleased` in chart/CHANGELOG.md before merging.

packageRules.description: chart/values.schema.json repeats the default of every value, and chart/tests/schema-test.sh fails while the two files disagree. Renovate changes the pin in values.yaml alone.
prBodyNotes: The job `chart-template-test` fails until `chart/values.schema.json` has the new default as well: run `scripts/schema-default.sh <key> <value>` on this branch, for example `scripts/schema-default.sh metrics.image.tag {{{newVersion}}}` or `scripts/schema-default.sh mariadb.image mariadb:{{{newVersion}}}`.

packageRules.description: A new MariaDB series upgrades the data directory of an existing installation on its first start: a deliberate move, its pull request carries the label decision.
One pull request per image moves its pin in chart/values.yaml and its entry in chart/Chart.yaml.

The PHP series of the base image moves by hand, never by the bot: the plugins of a site depend on it, and the base image has tags for series PHP has not released. The tag itself is a moving one on purpose: every release build pulls it afresh, and with it the current PHP patch release.
The documentation site's npm packages (site/), once a month; its pull requests build the site.
The override in site/package.json keeps VitePress 1 on a vite 6 that has the fixes. A new vite major comes with a VitePress release that asks for it, not on its own.
